name: Western Big Game Seasonal Habitat and Migration Corridors Fund
summary: Grants for restoring elk, mule deer and pronghorn seasonal habitat, stopover areas and migration corridors in western states, such as fence modification and sagebrush restoration. A separate option is open only to states and Tribes.

geography.label: Focal areas in 11 western states (18 states for Option B)

amount.note: Option A: most competitive grants are at least this much, with no maximum request

eligibility.rule: Project is prioritized under SO 3362 by a western state or by a Native nation
Option A project is in an eligible focal area in one of the 11 western states
Grant funds do not support ongoing legal compliance, except enhancements beyond baseline compliance

documents: State or Native nation wildlife agency director's support/acknowledgement letter
Statement of Litigation, unless a government applicant
Board of Trustees or Directors list
GAAP audited financial statements, if not current in Easygrants
IRS Form 990, if not current in Easygrants
Single Audit, if not current in Easygrants

applicant_types.quote: Eligible applicants include non-profit 501(c) organizations, U.S. Federal government agencies, state government agencies, local governments, municipal governments, Tribal Governments and organizations, and educational institutions.

geography.quote: Only projects proposed in focal areas identified by states under SO 3362 in 11 western states (depicted in green) and Native Nations within Arizona, California, Colorado, Idaho, Montana, Nevada, New Mexico, Oregon, Utah, Washington, and Wyoming will be eligible.

access.quote: is soliciting proposals for projects that improve the quality of ungulate seasonal habitat, stopover areas, and migration corridors

amount.quote: The most competitive grants will be at least $100,000 and there is no maximum request amount.

co_finance_required.quote: A minimum 1:1 non-federal match is required as in-kind or cash contributions.

effort.quote: Full Proposal Due Date April 21, 2026, 11:59 PM ET

eligibility.quote: Eligible projects will have been prioritized by one or several of 11 western states as a result of Interior Secretarial Order 3362 (SO 3362) or Native nations.

Only projects proposed in focal areas identified by states under SO 3362 in 11 western states (depicted in green) and Native Nations within Arizona, California, Colorado, Idaho, Montana, Nevada, New Mexico, Oregon, Utah, Washington, and Wyoming will be eligible.

NFWF funds may not be used to support ongoing efforts to comply with legal requirements, including permit conditions, mitigation and settlement agreements. However, grant funds may be used to support projects that enhance or improve upon existing baseline compliance efforts.

co_finance.quote: A minimum 1:1 non-federal match is required as in-kind or cash contributions.

documents.quote: To be considered for funding, all applications must be accompanied by a letter of support/acknowledgement from the director's office of the respective state or Native nation wildlife agency.
